answer: Optical physical unclonable functions curb Sybil attacks by binding agent identities to physical scattering tokens, such as a synthetic opal wafer. A network beacon broadcasts unpredictable optical queries, producing speckle patterns that adversaries cannot computationally mirror. Attackers must incur the verifiable capital cost of provisioning discrete photonic chips per identity. However, thermal fluctuations can distort speckle readings, causing false rejections.
